title: Prioritization Lab: lightweight experiment framework for monthly roadmap pivots
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
Create a lightweight, repeatable "Prioritization Lab" framework that lets PMs and cross-functional partners run short (2–4 week) experiments to validate priority shifts at the company OKR level, enabling monthly roadmap pivots without breaking delivery commitments.

Background:
We regularly get requests to re-prioritize company-level initiatives in response to new signals (customer escalations, market shifts, infra incidents). Full-scale re-planning is costly and disruptive. The goal of this ticket is to design a minimal experiment template, decision thresholds, and a telemetry/communication loop so leadership can make low-risk monthly adjustments anchored to measurable signals.

Scope:
- Define experiment template (hypothesis, owner, success metrics, rollback criteria, scope guardrails).
- Implement a one-click experiment creation form in the internal roadmap tool that wires into the metrics dashboard and flags affected deliverables.
- Provide runbook for Eng/Design/CS to adopt during experiments, including rapid rollbacks and temporary resource allocation rules.
- Create a lightweight view in the company roadmap showing active experiments and their impact on committed initiatives.

Out of scope:
- Replacing full-scale quarterly planning. This is meant to complement quarterly OKR cycles with fast, measured pivots.

Why now:
- Increasing frequency of short-term market signals (2H2025 onwards) and requests for faster course-correction.
- Early adopter PMs have run ad-hoc experiments with inconsistent telemetry; we need standardization to avoid conflicting cross-team actions.

Success definition (high-level):
A set of experiments run over the next 8 weeks that produce at least two validated priority adjustments (approve + commit or rollback) with clear telemetry and no unplanned customer regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment template (Confluence + roadmap-form) published and approved by product leadership
One-click experiment creation flows in internal roadmap tool that populate requirement fields for Eng/Design/CS
Metrics dashboard (Grafana) shows leading indicators for each running experiment and a single synthesized success score
Communication playbook documented (npm-style status, stakeholders list, rollback steps) and acknowledged by Eng, Design, and CS leads
Two pilot experiments executed end-to-end with learnings captured and a retro session scheduled
